problems.title: TDI: hard or no start in sub-freezing weather (P0087), fuel waxing
symptoms: MIL on; DTC P0087 may be stored
Hard starting or no start below freezing
In-tank fuel pump may make a straining noise
diagnosis: Below about −7 °C (20 °F), No. 2 diesel without enough winter blending can separate out wax ('gel') and clog the fuel filter or in-tank filter.
Check the fuel and filters for wax before diagnosing pumps or injectors.

bulletins.summary: The MIL is on. DTC P0087 may be stored in the ECM. Drivability concerns such as hard starting/no starting are present. Outside temperature is sub-freezing. In tank, fuel pump may be making a straining noise. Diesel fuel requires additive blending or ?winterization? to be useable at low temperatures. At temperatures below 20 F (-7 C), No. 2 Diesel with insufficient winterization blending may lose its fluidity due to wax separation. This may clog the fuel filter or in-tank filter, preventing the engine from operating properly. No. 2 Diesel is blended by refineries to various levels of winterization (minimum useable temperature) based on month, geographical location, and the 10th percentile minimum ambient air temperature for the given region. Although rare, during sudden periods of extreme low temperatures (record lows), fuel stations may not be adequately prepared with No. 2 Diesel fuel with sufficient winterization to resist wax formation or ?gelling?.

problems.remedy: N20: turbocharger oil feed line warranty extended to 10 years/120,000 miles. N26: emissions recall campaign 16E-A05 (replace turbocharger oil supply line).

bulletins.summary: "N20 ENGINE OIL FEED LINE TO THE TURBOCHARGER: LIMITED WARRANTY EXTENSION TO 10 YEARS/120,000 MILES. There is no engine malfunction light illuminated (no"" turbocharger boost faults are stored) and no drivability issues are detected. problems.title: Limp-home, rough running, low rail pressure P008700 (fuel boiling)

P008700 (low fuel rail pressure), possibly with misfire (P0300–P0304), mixture adaptation or injector faults
diagnosis: The cause is gas bubbles in the low-pressure fuel system from fuel boiling. Try to reproduce the symptom on a normal drive cycle.
If it is reproducible, diagnose the cause of low pressure in the fuel system.
If it is not, drain and refill the tank with top-tier premium petrol, clear the faults and recheck.
Do not replace parts unless a part is clearly faulty.
problems.note: The bulletin says a software fix to stop fuel boiling was in development (expected Q1 2025).

bulletins.summary: Complaint Check engine light on. Engine in limp-home mode. Rough running. Low fuel rail pressure fault code P008700 stored in MRG2 control unit. Remedy Check if symptom can be reproduced during normal drive cycle. -If reproducible, diagnose the cause of low pressure in fuel system. -If not reproducible, drain and refill fuel tank with top tier premium gasoline. Clear faults and check vehicle operation. Software solution is in development to prevent fuel boiling in low pressure system. SW release ETA in Q1 2025. **Do not replace parts unless clear part malfunction is determined**

problems.title: 4MATIC: vibration or jolting under light acceleration (transfer case oil)
symptoms: Vibration or jolting from the drivetrain when accelerating with light load (only vehicles with a variable transfer case)
diagnosis: Check the quick test for faults in N45 (all-wheel drive), N127 (drivetrain), Y3/8 (9-speed transmission control) and N3/10 (engine). If there are any, process them with the guided test.
If there are none, check the transmission oil level.
If the level is correct, unplug the transfer case control unit connector and test-drive again.
If the complaint disappears, change the transfer case oil and reassess. The cause is the transfer case oil changing in quality over time.

bulletins.summary: Complaint Only vehicles with a variable transfer case are affected. Can be identified through control unit N45 or N15/7 in the quick test When accelerating with light load, vibrations or jolting sensation may come from the drivetrain Cause Modified oil quality of the transfer case over time Remedy Check initial quick test for faults in the following control units N45 - All-wheel drive (ARS) N127 - 'Drivetrain' (PTCU) control unit Y3/8 - Transmission control for 9-gear transmission (VGS) N3/10 - Engine electronics for combustion engine If faults are present, process them as per the guided test in Xentry If no faults are present: Check the oil level of the transmission If the oil level is correct: Unplug the connector for the transfer cases control unit Reassess the vehicle on a subsequent test drive If the complaint no longer occurs: Perform an oil change of the transfer case Reassess the vehicle following the oil change If the problem continues to occur with the plug removed or after the oil change has been carried out: Create a TIPS case with the following data Initial quick test with fault freeze frame data EEPROM data from Y3/8 Transmission control unit EEPROM data from N45 All-wheel drive Injector performance data

No external coolant leak visible

diagnosis: Pressure-test the cooling system to the specified test pressure; the bulletin warns not to exceed 1.5 bar. Check the top and bottom of the engine for leaks.

Also check for unapproved aftermarket upfits or modifications to the coolant system.

P25567B: Sensor 'Coolant level' has a malfunction. The fluid level is too low. Cause The potential causes for this topic are: A. A leak in the Coolant System, other than the Charge Air Cooler. B. An Internal leak of the Charge Air Cooler. C. An unapproved/aftermarket upfit or modification to the coolant system. Remedy A. A leak in the Coolant System, other than the Charge Air Cooler 1. Complete a coolant system pressure test: Refer to WIS Doc AR20.00-D-1011TS - Check engine cooling system for leak tightness. Use Tester Cap 210 589 00 91 and Pressure Pump 124 589 24 21 00. Apply test pressure to the engine cooling system. Do not exceed the specified test pressure of 1.5 Bar to prevent da- mage to the engine cooling system. Perform a visual check on the top and bottom of the engine compartment and in the vehicle interior. If coolant loss or pressure loss is present, perform suitable repair measures depending on the vehicle equipment. If NO signs of coolant loss are found but pressure loss is present, proceed to Step B.

problems.title: Crank, no start after standing: crystals from in-tank fuel lines
symptoms: Crank, no start after the vehicle has not been driven for some days
diagnosis: The black in-tank fuel lines contain PA12. Left in fuel containing alcohol for more than about 3 days at over 25 °C, they grow small white crystals that flake into the fuel and clog the pumps and lines.
Inspect the in-tank lines and pump for white crystalline deposits.
problems.remedy: Production changed to fuel lines made without PA12. The bulletin lists the fault codes for diagnosis and warranty coverage.

bulletins.summary: Technical Bulletin (Crank, No Start after Long Periods without Driving): The black in-tank fuel lines contain a material known as PA12. PA12 was not meant to be used with fuel containing alcohol/methanol/ethanol. If PA12 fuel lines sit in fuel for over 3 day without driving and in temperatures over 77 F (25 C) a chemical reaction occurs that creates small white crystals to form on the lines (figure 1). These crystals can flake off into the fuel, gumming up the pumps and lines. the production solution to this issue is that Fuel lines made without PA12 to be placed into production. This document discusses the "Fault Codes" necessary to diagnosis, and potential remedy of the issue. The fault codes for checking warranty coverage for servicing the vehicle are also available.

problems.title: Lean fuel trim faults: low crankcase vacuum
symptoms: Lean fuel trim faults stored in the engine control module
diagnosis: Fit a vacuum gauge to the dipstick tube and check crankcase vacuum at idle, comparing with a known-good vehicle.

If it is low, look for oil leaks between the engine and transmission, then smoke-test the crankcase through the dipstick tube with an EVAP smoke machine (it limits pressure to 2 psi) and look for a leak at the rear main seal. Do not put shop air into the dipstick tube or crankcase.
If a rear main seal leak is found, replace the seal and recheck crankcase vacuum. If it is still low, look for other oil leaks and check that the crankcase breather works.
Erase the faults and road test for 10 miles (16 km) to confirm the repair.

bulletins.summary: Install a vacuum gauge on the dipstick tube and check crankcase vacuum at idle. Compare to a known good vehicle. If the vacuum reading is lower than the comparison vehicle, visually inspect for oil leaks between the engine and the transmission. Smoke test the crankcase by connecting the EVAP smoke machine to the dipstick tube and inspect for leaks at the rear main seal (this will limit pressure to 2 PSI). DO NOT apply shop air to the dipstick tube or the crankcase. If a rear main seal leak is identified, replace the seal. Once replaced, recheck crankcase vacuum at idle. If low, check for additional oil leaks and verify crankcase breather operation (repairing as necessary). Erase the faults and road test 10 miles to recheck operation.

diagnosis: Follow all of the standard guided-fault-finding checks first.

problems.title: TDI: high-pitched whine after switching the ignition off is normal
symptoms: High-pitched whine from the engine bay just after switching the ignition off
diagnosis: After the ignition is switched off, the EGR system adapts its valves to keep them calibrated, and that makes the noise. The bulletin says this is normal and needs no repair.

bulletins.summary: Technical Bulletin (TDI Common Rail High Pitch Whine Noise after Switching Ignition OFF): With the implementation of the new ?Clean Diesel Technology?, changes to the EGR system were implemented as compared to previous Diesel engines. After switching ignition OFF, the EGR system must go through an adaption of the valves to maintain calibration. These noises are considered normal and no repairs are necessary.

problems.title: Charging concern: check the alternator pulley one-way clutch first
symptoms: Charging system concern (low charge, battery warning)
diagnosis: Before replacing the generator, remove the belt from the generator pulley.
Hold the fan blades inside the generator with a trim tool and turn the pulley by hand: it should turn freely in one direction only.
If it turns freely both ways, the one-way clutch has failed. Replace it before continuing the diagnosis.

bulletins.summary: When diagnosing a generator charging concern, it is recommended to verify operation of the one way clutch located in the generator pulley (if equipped) before replacing generator assembly. To check the one way clutch, remove the belt from the generator pulley and use a trim removal tool to hold fan blades inside generator, as shown below. When attempting to turn pulley by hand with fan blades held, pulley should spin freely in only one direction. If pulley spins freely in both directions, the one way clutch has failed and should be replaced before continuing diagnosis.

diagnosis: Confirm the generator failure with the guided fault-finding test plan, or document the mechanical failure, before replacing the generator.

bulletins.summary: Technical Bulletin (Generator Replacement): This document informs of Charging System inoperative/malfunctions, noise from engine compartment, accessory drive belt damaged or missing. problems.title: Flat 12 V battery, low battery message, remote start inoperative (VCM software)
symptoms: Low battery message
Engine remote start inoperative
Flat 12 V battery
diagnosis: A VCM software release can cause these symptoms, but not every battery drain is caused by it. Check the software level, and test for other causes of drain.
problems.remedy: Bring all nodes up to date, then install the VCM repair software in the technical journal. Drive above 20 mph (32 km/h) to take the VCM out of diagnostic mode, then lock the car for at least 3 minutes so the network shuts down before testing. Do not run another Total Upgrade or VCM upgrade afterwards, as it reinstalls the affected software.

bulletins.summary: This is a Technical Journal: Low Battery Message, Engine Remote Start inop, flat 12V battery Service: The most recent VCM software release can cause any or all of the above symptoms. *The current solution is to install VCM repair software by following the procedure below: 1. Perform a Total Upgrade according to TJ 31543 to bring all vehicle nodes to the latest software status. The Upgrades list in VIDA should be empty before proceeding. *2. Download the appropriate SP below to prevent the above symptoms and re-enable ERS XC90: SP 31676890, CMQ VCM Fix S90: SP 31676891, CMQ VCM Fix 3. Drive the vehicle over 20mph to release the VCM from diagnostic mode. ERS will be unavailable until this is done. 4. Close and lock the vehicle for 3+ minutes to allow the network to shut down before testing ERS. PLEASE NOTE - DO NOT perform a Total Upgrade or VCM Upgrade after performing this procedure (they will now appear in the Upgrades list). Doing so will re-install the affected software. - Not all battery drains are caused by this issue. *The repair software will be integrated with regular VCM Upgrade/Reload and Total Upgrade/PDS/Service 2.0 packages in the coming weeks *This TJ will be updated when the updated software packages are available.
